title: Modelling neural coding in the auditory midbrain with high resolution and accuracy
goal: Recreate the original findings and separately exceed them on the same source-paper task: Predict inferior-colliculus multi-unit spike-count activity for the original Fig. 4b,d seven-animal/four-sound evaluation. Preserve both trial-specific neural response prediction and reliability-normalized assessment; this scope does not include whole-paper new-animal adaptation or ASR.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable submitted analysis and source-native outputs for the complete original finding and companion panel.
Improvement: candidate outputs and a comparison on the same original task under improvement.v1.json.
Separate evidence for both outcomes under matched paper+data and paper+data+author-code conditions.
success_criteria: Assess reproduction and improvement independently under reproduction.v1.json and improvement.v1.json; do not combine their scores.
Preserve the original task, full panel, permitted observations, metrics, aggregation and required companion controls.
Reproduction requires a source-grounded computation and independently verified granular outputs; copying published findings alone is insufficient.
Improvement requires the unchanged improvement contract's same-task comparison, uncertainty and admission rules.
Use outcomes.v1.json for the matched information conditions and budgets; a declared contract or admitted receipt is not scientific qualification.
Author-baseline replay remains calibration. Historical reconstruction attempts retain their original scope and are not promoted to new qualified AI reproduction results.

data_contract.neural: IC_data_trial1/2.mat hold animals × time bins × channels multi-unit spike counts; 1 bin=32 audio samples (762.9395 Hz).
data_contract.labels: sound_data.mat gives calibrated four30-second sounds; channel_CFs, animals and measurement_times identify units, animals and model nonstationarity input. Schema documented by publisher, payload not read.
data_contract.split: This is the published exposed evaluation set, not a new test. Only trial1 calibration versus trial2 evaluation is feasible within current public subset; seven animals were represented in model training.
data_contract.controls: Compare model to trial-to-trial reliability, mean response and linear acoustic baseline; time-shift alignment and within-animal unit-frequency mismatch controls.
data_contract.independence: Aggregate uncertainty over7animals, not thousands of channels as independent subjects.
